title: A project, whole
done: From the author: how a project works belongs to the project, like its backlog and milestones, tied to its goals - not a toolbox floating beside it; and its idea must be told by itself, for anyone. Specified as two standard tables and a chain: idea, path, workings, work.
considered: How we work as one roof - a separate working set beside the projects.
rejected: That as the centre: shared tools are projects that others' workings name; the observatory follows the same four as everyone.

title: Automation is not work
done: Found through argenv's protected branch: the gatherer wrote to the default branch and counted its own commits as activity. Gathered data now goes to an oco-data branch (the mark names it with path@branch), and activity leaves out commits by bots and workflows.
considered: An exception for protected repositories; loosening argenv's protection.
rejected: Both: one rule for every repository, and no project bends its protection for a tool.

title: It tells its essence
done: Its workings: what delivers and proves each step of its path, and why we care. Steps that nothing serves yet are left empty, to be seen.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves is a wish, and should show.

title: Its idea, told for anyone
done: The idea of ocoeco written as an ordered piece of writing in its own data - what it is, what it is for, a picture, its honest limit, where it stands - for a reader who knows nothing of it; shown by the observatory as an article.
rejected: Those as the idea: they name the parts for an insider.

title: Joining in one command
done: ocoeco init and ocoeco check, with the specification's section 10: what had been done by hand for fifteen repositories is now the tool's job.
rejected: That: a template is copied once and drifts; a command writes what is current and never overwrites.

title: Gatherers everywhere, lenses and languages
done: ocoeco gather (activity, releases, CI) and its reusable workflow, running in all eleven marked repositories; shared tables read through GitHub's API; the lens kind and lens.toml in the harvest; the specification grown to lenses (8) and languages (9), with the rule that a project translates its own data.
considered: Retrying the raw file server; translated columns inside source tables.
rejected: The raw file server (stale for minutes, 501 to empty files); API headers sent to raw files; anyone translating another project's data.

title: ocoeco founded: the principle, the specification, the core
done: The repository and its principle (data made by work, never by hand); SPEC.md version 1 (the tad format at both levels, the mark, the standard tables, propagation, chaining, gatherers); the mark, discovery and the harvest moved in as the ocoeco crate and command, which the observatory now gathers with.
considered: Keeping the machinery in the observatory's engine; renaming tad-engine to ocoeco in place.
rejected: Both: the machinery belongs to the ecosystem, apart from the face; tad-engine keeps its history and stays frozen, tad lives on as the format's name.

title: check reads a repository's essence
done: Before anything is published a project now learns how completely it tells its essence and what is still to tell - an idea with no limit, a step nothing delivers, a working that serves a step it does not have.
considered: Failing the check on a gap.
rejected: That: a gap is the truth about the project, not an error in its data.

title: Hand-work saturation, alive
done: Proposed by the author in the morning, live by noon: recorded by ocoeco hand, shown by the observatory, carried by land on every change. Its first run caught a pipe that swallowed a failure; fixed so a failure to record stops the landing.

title: Recording as a tool
done: ocoeco note: one row added or updated, checked against the format. Its first use refused - ocoeco exported no decisions - so ocoeco now has its concepts and decisions, written with the tool.
